unresolved_uncertainty.what: Routed read-form question: instances recorded, not adjudicated. Seven read forms are rendered across this cluster (MT 35:9, MT 35:12, two at MT 36:13, two at MT 36:14, one at MT 36:15). None occurs in the running-text extract, which carries the written forms; each reconstructs its witness note entry exactly once the morpheme separator is removed; 3 of the 7 entries carry a separator and 4 carry none. I reproduce none of the seven and name the sites instead.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the two sub-cases are not one question — a separator removed from an entry that has one is a rendering choice, while an entry that never had one cannot have been stripped, which is the narrower point the MT 35:9/35:12/36:13/36:14 findings rest on. The toolkit's own tier description, which accepts a read form from the note layer when a K/Q keyword stands within 160 characters and compares against the note's raw split bytes, is the nearest sanctioning language I found.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The per-cluster flag listing handed to this lane is incomplete for c17. It lists one refs_mirror flag on each of five rows; the digest-bound suite also carries, standing on these same six rows, one web_quotes flag and nineteen universals flags. Those members identify their flags by row position while refs_mirror identifies by decision_id, and only the decision_id member was attributed.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: a reviewer answering only the listed flags would not see the web_quotes flag on the MT 36:16-36:23 row (answered in that row's item). If the attribution gap holds across the plan, every cluster is short the members that key their flags the other way.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row must disclose a non-variant editorial note carried by a verse inside its span. The witness carries such a note on MT 36:7 (an accent read differently from the printed edition), and the row covering MT 36:1-36:12 cites MT 36:7 as evidence without disclosing it. The note layer is described as single-witness apparatus to be disclosed, but the corpus is not uniform: of 36 rows whose spans cover such a note, 26 disclose and 10 do not. I did not score it against the row.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: it decides whether a low finding stands on that row and on the nine others that are silent; cheaper to rule once than per row.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The refs_mirror flags on five rows are answered as legitimate with one exception I did not score: the row covering MT 36:24-36:32 lists MT 11:19 in its boundary-evidence field, a lexical contrast twenty-five chapters away bearing on neither of its seams, and the mirror check did not catch it.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: whether a cross-chapter lexical contrast may sit in a boundary-evidence field is a filing convention rather than a fact about the text, so it is not mine to decide; but the mirror check evidently does not see it, which matters before that check is relied on as complete.
